current: OntologyRegistry (backend/crates/libs/qip-agents/src/registries.rs) holds OntologyTypeSpec definitions (qip-contracts::expansion: family, name, version, schema, description) keyed by (family, name, version) in a BTreeMap, for all eight families of OntologyTypeFamily (entity, event, relationship, market, asset, product, causal_driver, lifecycle). register() runs OntologyTypeSpec::validate, so version 0 (a stored type carrying no version) is refused; it refuses an exact duplicate and any version not above the latest already held for that name, so a late-arriving old definition cannot displace the current one. get_type(family, name, version) returns that version's own definition; get_latest and types_by_family read the highest version. current: Criteria::score computes priority = feasibility x merit x (1 + novelty), where merit is economic value per unit of cost plus the seven other unitless inputs. Novelty multiplies and never adds, so a candidate with maximum novelty and zero on every other input has a priority of exactly zero, below any candidate with positive economic value and information gain, and two candidates with equal novelty rank by the rest. The DISCOVER queue's own importance x confidence x novelty rule is unchanged.
verification: cargo test -p qip-expansion --test expansion novelty_alone_never_outranks_a_candidate_with_economic_value_and_information_gain
notes: Closed 2026-10-05 as a library: qip-expansion has no production caller, so integrated stays false. No composition root builds a queue because no detector in the tree states a severity or an economic value for what it finds and nothing measures most of the eleven criteria; wiring it would mean inventing them. The property is checked over 2,000 generated candidates, a quarter of them carrying value and information gain and nothing else, and once through the queue with the tie-break set against the valued candidate. Mutation fired and was restored: novelty added to merit instead of multiplying it.

current: The export exists, and it is synchronous with the reflex loop. qip-edge's CellUplink publishes a CellStateDelta every tick carrying the last pass's fills, refusals and reconciliation breaks - regional reflex experience - bounded per delta (MAX_FILLS_PER_DELTA, MAX_REFUSALS_PER_DELTA=64, with *_omitted counters), behind a circuit breaker, with a 64-entry in-memory dead-letter queue (qip-edge/src/mesh.rs; qip-edge-node/src/mesh.rs). qip-api drains those deltas into Platform::ingest_cell_report (qip-api/src/mesh.rs:1621), whose refusals feed the feasibility window a venue is withdrawn on - central learning from regional experience. But qip-edge-node's serve loop runs the mesh exchange and Cell::work on the same thread, exchange first (main.rs:858-890; the node's own doc at main.rs:88-104 says so), with ClientLimits::default() on the link (mesh.rs:119: 2 s connect, 15 s read). A centre that accepts and then stalls therefore holds the next reflex pass for up to the read timeout per call until the breaker opens: a synchronous dependency of the hot path on the global sink, which this requirement forbids.
evidence: backend/crates/apps/qip-edge-node/src/main.rs:88-104 (serve runs the halt poll, journal flush, mesh exchange and Cell::work on the same thread)
backend/crates/apps/qip-edge-node/tests/mesh.rs:375 a_tick_against_an_unreachable_centre_reports_it_and_leaves_the_cell_running (a refused connection only - fails fast; no stalled-peer test)
gap: Experience export must move off the pass thread (or be made non-blocking) so a stalled centre cannot delay a pass, with a bounded local buffer of exported episodes that reports when full. Today the only buffer is the dead-letter queue of superseding deltas, not an episode buffer, and no test stalls the sink while the cell trades and measures pass latency.
verification: No test demonstrates the required property. cargo test -p qip-edge-node --test mesh a_tick_against_an_unreachable_centre_reports_it_and_leaves_the_cell_running covers only a refused connection. Needed: a chaos test with a peer that accepts and never answers, asserting pass cadence and decisions are unchanged and the export buffer reports when full.
notes: ADR 0008's 'cells decide alone' is a real, structural architectural property (Cell::work does not block on centre reachability for its own trading decisions today), which is favourable groundwork, but the specific reflex-experience export and its bounded buffer do not exist to verify against. verify: MISSING -> INCORRECT. The assessor said no export mechanism exists; the mesh uplink exports fills, refusals and breaks every tick and the centre learns from them. It runs synchronously before Cell::work on the node's single serve thread with a 15 s read timeout - the synchronous hot-path dependency the requirement names. deployable=false: qip-edge-node is not deployed (execution_nodes = {} everywhere). tested=false: no test exercises a stall.

current: Two of the requirement's clauses hold for the one memory kind the platform writes. EpisodicMemory (qip-ai/src/memory/store.rs) holds at most its capacity, refuses a duplicate episode id at remember (store.rs:347-354), and its EpisodeSampler (sampler.rs) gives up calm episodes before surprising ones, so high-value (high-surprise) episodes outlive calm ones and growth stays bounded. It is live on Platform and written every LEARN pass. Nothing summarises or compresses: growth is bounded by eviction, not by consolidating many entries into a smaller abstraction. Semantic lessons (qip-agents ResearchMemory) are unbounded and never written in production; procedural, market and failure memories do not exist.
evidence: backend/crates/libs/qip-ai/src/memory/sampler.rs:1-40 (the eviction seam: dense at high surprise, sparse in calm)
gap: No summarisation, compression or abstraction of stored memory; deduplication is exact-id refusal at admission, not merging of near-duplicate content; no consolidation pass over a stored set; and only the episodic kind is bounded at all.
verification: cargo test -p qip-ai --test episodic (19 tests, incl. the two above). No test runs consolidation over duplicate and stale episodes, because no consolidation exists.
notes: Priority P3 per the requirement's notes (a master Phase 9 exit); EpisodicMemory's existing capacity-based eviction is a reasonable foundation to extend rather than a competing mechanism. verify: upgraded MISSING -> PARTIAL. 'High-value episodes are kept and memory growth stays bounded' is delivered and tested for episodic memory (value-graded eviction plus duplicate-id refusal); the consolidation verbs - summarise, compress, merge duplicates - are absent, which the gap states.
